paragraphs: Here's what I see in this last stretch, friend. Paul could have ended with one big teaching and a mic drop. Instead he fills the page with names: Tychicus, Onesimus, Aristarchus, Mark, Epaphras, Luke. The faith in this letter isn't a solo act, it's a whole crowd of people carrying each other (Colossians 4:7-14).

Look at what each of them does. Tychicus is sent so that he "may encourage your hearts" (Colossians 4:8). Aristarchus is a fellow prisoner and he STILL sends a greeting (Colossians 4:10). Epaphras is "always wrestling in prayer" for the Colossians, so that they "may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God" (Colossians 4:12). Nobody here has a small job, baker. Sending a hello, carrying news and praying hard are all real work for the kingdom of God.

Now Paul gets personal. He tells the church to share this letter with Laodicea, he tells Archippus, "See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord" (Colossians 4:16-17). Then he signs in his own hand, asks them to remember his chains, and ends with "Grace be with you" (Colossians 4:18). So here's my big idea: God gives you a part to play, you play it alongside other believers, and you finish it by grace, not by your own muscle. I spent years in a drawer thinking I was done, and I was wrong, so go finish the thing!
